parsed.explanation: The division is strongly protective: broad gender-identity non-discrimination covering public accommodations, hate-crime penalties since 1999, panic-defence repeal, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, shield laws enforceable against out-of-state action, and settled partner recognition. But the combined regime includes a hostile federal layer the traveller cannot avoid: the Feb 2025 visa cable telling officers to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility (prompting advisories from ≥8 foreign governments), passport-marker restrictions upheld Nov 2025, a federal ban on trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities, documented abuse of trans people in federal immigration custody, and federal hostility toward minors' care. No criminalisation of identity, functioning courts, and pending challenges hold the score near the middle-upper band rather than lower.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, with consideration of a fraud-based lifetime ineligibility finding; X markers ceased; Nov 2025 Supreme Court let passport restrictions take effect; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated; ≥8 foreign governments issued travel advisories by Mar–Apr 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; civil-liberties union suit pending; entry not automatically barred.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening is federal and precedes any state protection; a discrepancy at the border never reaches state public-accommodation coverage.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse by guards. National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State hate-crime law adds penalties for gender-identity motivation; functioning courts; shield laws; state panic-defence repealed 2021.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State remedies are unreachable once a visitor is inside federal custody; custody placement practice is federally directed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (airports, federal buildings, federally funded schools) — a universal exposure for any outed visitor. Nationally, 9+1 states ban gender-congruent facility use in all government buildings; 4 states make it criminal.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no documented facility ban and has required gender-neutral single-user bathrooms since 2018; listed most-protective on non-discrimination.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding condition reaches into this protective state's federally funded settings; the map warns other sex-definition laws may still affect access.

care_services.exposure: Federal layer: Jan 2025 order framing minors' care as 'mutilation', DOJ subpoenas of under-19 patient records, proposed Oct 2025 insurance rule barring reimbursement for under-18 trans care, funding threats; care banned in 27 states.
care_services.protection: State shield laws (2023, 2024) enforceable against out-of-state action; insurers required to cover trans care since 2013; conversion therapy on minors prohibited; education department protects trans students.
care_services.interaction: Shield law protects a care-seeking family in-state, but cannot prevent federal investigation, subpoenas or funding withdrawal.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ Dec 2025 reward memo pairing 'radical gender ideology' with violent extremism; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Jan 2025 order directing law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology' in schools; 2025 poll: 66% back birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 national employment-discrimination ruling; state hate-crime law since 1999; memo does not list 'radical gender ideology' as a reward criterion and states CT powers won't target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises the probability and social licence of adverse encounters even where state law protects.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 2025 order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; sports bans; proposed federal insurance rule; facility bans in schools in 21+ units; DOJ record subpoenas reach a travelling family's medical data.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield laws, insurance-coverage mandate, anti-bullying law covering gender identity, 2023 education-department policy defending trans students, no documented state school facility ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor is exposed to federal scrutiny and care-refusal risk that state shield law cannot fully offset; state inquiry risk is low but federal data collection is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National bias-crime statistics show sustained anti-LGBTQ bias incidents; a trans student was arrested and held in a men's ward in another unit (Mar 2025) — showing enforcement of facility laws elsewhere.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalties for gender identity since 1999; public-accommodations coverage for hotels, restaurants, shops; panic defence repealed; national hate-crime statute. Denominators/trans-specific rates not supplied.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street hostility in this division meets a complaint machinery that exists, though enforcement data is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple federal orders blocked then revived, litigation unresolved — exposure varies by travel date; no state enforcement data for hate-crime or public-accommodations provisions; no data on shield-law operation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several orders; civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ, running equality and identity-document trackers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but uneven: federal litigation is slow, while state complaint routes are documented but untested in the sources.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above this anchor: no detention pipeline for visitors, no entry bars executed as routine cell detention, no torture, no credible capital exposure, and courts grant real relief. Federal custody abuse exists but only after an arrest, unlike this anchor's routine post-inspection imprisonment with judges deferring to police summaries.

Similar in kind at the border: discretionary secondary screening, humiliation, refusal of entry, slow and rarely revised remedies. Ours adds a documented lifetime-fraud referral and multi-government advisories, but offsets this with strong in-country public-accommodation and hate-crime protection that this anchor lacks — net position comparable, slightly below.

Lower than this anchor: care access and remedies are strong in the division, but a federal layer imposes facility exclusion, document-refusal policy, custody hostility and active threats to minors' care with litigation unresolved. The 0.85 case assumes care guarantees with only rural gaps; here guarantees coexist with an operative federal hostility the traveller cannot opt out of.

Well above this anchor: no documented birth-sex prison housing for visitors here beyond federal custody exposure, no cross-dressing offence, and identity-based arrest is documented only in another unit. Its slow remedies and criminalisation of presentation in administrative buildings place it a clear tier below this division's operative package.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes stacked. In-state, everyday exposure is genuinely low: hotels, restaurants and shops are covered by a 2007 public-accommodations law, hate-crime penalties and a repealed panic defence apply, single-user bathrooms are gender-neutral, and shield laws protect a family seeking care. Around that sits a federal layer the traveller cannot pass: sex-doubt visa refusal with a fraud-referral option, passport-marker restrictions upheld in Nov 2025, exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities, documented abuse in federal immigration custody, and hostile framing toward trans people and minors' care. Litigation is live and several orders are enjoined, so outcomes vary by date. The result is low street-level severity but repeated universal federal exposures — placing the combined regime in the elevated middle of the scale.
